title: Notice to all Taxpayers Subject to the Southaven Tourism and Convention Tax for the city of Southaven
text:
MISSISSIPPI DEPARTMENT OF REVENUE
Sales and Use Tax Bureau Notice 72-26-03 March 11, 2026
NOTICE TO ALL TAXPAYERS SUBJECT TO THE SOUTHAVEN TOURISM AND
CONVENTION TAX FOR THE CITY OF SOUTHAVEN
House Bill 1618, passed during the 1993 Regular Session of the Mississippi Legislature, authorized a
special tax to be levied on certain businesses located in the corporate limits of the City of Southaven,
Mississippi. The Bill levies a one percent (1%) tax on the gross income of hotels and motels within the
corporate limits of the City of Southaven.
On February 3, 2026, the Mayor and the Board of Alderman of the City of Southaven adopted, by resolution,
their intent to recognize and adopt the updated statutory definition of “hotel” provided in Senate Bill 2805,
as passed during the 2025 Regular Session of the Mississippi Legislature, which includes entities and
individuals furnishing, facilitating, arranging, brokering, or providing transient guest accommodations,
including third-party facilitators and short-term rental platforms. This updated definition shall apply to all
special levy tax collections authorized by the City under its Local and Private Law and supersedes any
conflicting definition of “hotel” or “motel” contained in such Local and Private Law, including any
minimum room requirement greater than one (1), recognizing that state law applies to the levy to any
number of rooms, including one (1). The effective date of the imposition shall be April 1, 2026, recognizing
that Senate Bill 2805 has been in force since July 1, 2025.
*** Note – Hotels and Motels within the City of Southaven will collect the one percent (1%)
Southaven Tourism and Convention Tax, the two percent (2%) Desoto County Convention Tourist
Promotion Tax and the seven percent (7%) retail rate of tax for a total of ten percent (10%).
For purposes of this levy, the terms “hotel" or "motel" means any establishment engaged in the business of
furnishing or providing rooms intended or designed for dwelling, lodging or sleeping purposes to transient
guests. The term “hotel” or “motel” does not include any hospital, convalescent or nursing home or
sanitarium, or any hotel-like facility operated by or in connection with a hospital or medical clinic providing
rooms exclusively for patients and their families.
IMPORTANT INFORMATION FOR HOTELS AND MOTELS: Beginning April 1, 2026, continue
reporting the seven percent (7%) sales tax using rate code 74. The Desoto County Convention Tourist
Promotion Tax of two percent (2%) and the additional one percent (1%) tax on hotels and motels should be
reported as a combined rate of three percent (3%) using rate cade 94.
